item.research_question: How can a multistage mechanical alloying strategy be designed to construct nanocrystalline high-entropy alloys with large aspect ratios and thin intergranular amorphous layers to achieve temperature-stable broadband megahertz electromagnetic wave absorption?
item.processing_route: Multistage mechanical alloying (MMA) consisting of dry milling (0-30 h, argon atmosphere, no process control agent) followed by wet milling (3-10 h, 40 mL anhydrous ethanol). Key parameters: ball-to-powder mass ratio 20:1, large ball (10 mm) to small ball (6 mm) ratio 1:2, 4 min pause every 30 min. Optimal sample D20: 20 h dry milling + 5 h wet milling.
item.test_conditions: Electromagnetic properties measured at -50 to 150 °C in the MHz frequency range; Corrosion resistance tested in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution; Magnetic properties (VSM) measured from 30 to 840 °C; Reflection loss calculated for D20/SiO2 composites (8:2 mass ratio) with thicknesses of 1-5 mm.
key_findings: The D20 sample (20 h dry + 5 h wet) achieved a single-phase face-centered cubic (FCC) structure with high crystallinity.
The average intergranular amorphous layer thickness of the D20 sample was less than 2 nm.
The D20 sample exhibited a Curie temperature of 774 °C.
The maximum reflection loss (RL) of D20/SiO2 composites (8:2 mass ratio, 5 mm thickness) was greater than -7 dB.
The electromagnetic wave absorption bandwidth (RL < -7 dB) maintained between 523 and 600 MHz from -50 to 150 °C.
The corrosion current density (icorr) of the D20 sample was 7.0 μA cm−2.
The charge transfer resistance (Rct) of the D20 sample was 3,739 Ω in 3.5 wt% NaCl solution.
The D20 sample showed a smaller permeability temperature coefficient compared to samples with different milling times.
item.mechanism: The phase transition from BCC to amorphous to FCC occurs primarily during dry milling, with the FCC phase providing superior ductility for flattening during wet milling. The resulting large aspect ratios break the Snoek's limit and enhance planar anisotropy, while the thin intergranular amorphous layers (<2 nm) facilitate strong magnetic coupling between nanograins, leading to high and temperature-stable permeability. The 'cocktail effect' of the HEA elements contributes to high corrosion resistance and high Curie temperature.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study, though it notes that excessive wet milling time leads to serious crushing of particles and that high temperatures (150 °C) can cause a slight decrease in absorption performance due to increased permittivity affecting impedance matching.
item.future_work: The authors state the work provides a facile and tunable strategy to design MHz electromagnetic absorbers with temperature stability, broadband, and resistance to harsh environments, implying future application in such environments, but do not explicitly list specific future research directions beyond the general utility of the strategy.
quotes: FeCoNiCr0.4Cu0.2 HEAs with dry milling 20 h and wet milling 5 h (D20) exhibit higher and more stable permeability because of larger aspect ratios and thinner intergranular amorphous layers.

The maximum reflection loss (RL) of D20/SiO2 composites is greater than − 7 dB with 5 mm thickness, and EMW absorption bandwidth (RL < − 7 dB) can maintain between 523 and 600 MHz from − 50 to 150 °C.
